disclosures.reason: want-zero AllocsPerRun assert over a point addition plus scalar/point encode round-trips: Go's escape analysis proves every Point, Scalar and field-element temporary non-escaping (even NewIdentityPoint()/NewGeneratorPoint() stay on the stack), while the managed model heap-boxes each one, so zero is structurally unreachable. RE-PINNED AT 1.24.13 from crypto/internal/edwards25519.TestAllocations: the H10 relocation moves the declaration into crypto/internal/fips140test under this name, and the roster's relocation record expects `class` and `signature` to survive VERBATIM -- they do, which is the zero-re-signs measurement holding for the right reason, the signature never having moved. Re-measured at the pass-2 tip: the run reports `counted 7,500 go2cs-runtime object allocations (698,400 bytes) over 100 run(s)` = 75 per run, an allocation COUNT in Go's own units (the go2cs counter SAW them), which is the COUNT arm of the 2026-09-05 ladder; the proof above is the stated floor that makes it structural rather than deferred.

disclosures.name: TestXAESAllocations
disclosures.reason: want-zero AllocsPerRun assert over an xaesSeal + xaesOpen round trip (xaes_test.go:19-37). The measured closure allocates five local slices per run -- key 32, nonce 24, plaintext 16, aad 16, ciphertext cap 32 -- plus the per-call AES/GCM and XAES-KDF state, none of which escapes, so Go's escape analysis keeps every one off the heap while golib necessarily boxes them. Reading: `counted 1,990 go2cs-runtime object allocations (157,600 bytes) over 10 run(s)` = 199 per run, and the run's own note states the figure is an allocation COUNT per run from go2cs's runtime counter, the structural mirror of runtime.MemStats.Mallocs, over golib sites only and therefore a LOWER BOUND. STRUCTURAL rather than deferred: no named mechanism removes those allocations (golib has no stack allocation for a slice) and a lower bound can only rise, never approach the want. This is the pin authored in C1's classing record (docs/phase4/CENSUS-fips140test-divergence-classing.md) and is reused here verbatim.
